To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ABAC is not a new access control model but a new way of specifying and configuring access control policies for existing models, (2) DAC, MAC and role based access control (RBAC) are all special cases of attribute based access control, and (3) the three existing access control models are not mutually exclusive but can be combined in many ways to form hybrid models.

(a) DAC is a special case of MAC, (b) DAC and MAC are special cases of RBAC, (c) RBAC is a special case ABAC, (d) ABAC is not a special case of DAC or MAC, and (e) ABAC is more expressive than DAC, MAC and even RBAC.
ABAC is a superset of DAC and MAC and that RBAC is a special case of MAC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a unified ABAC model that is a superset of DAC, MAC and flat/hierarchical RBAC.
the following questions: What are the key features that distinguish ABAC from other models?
the question “How can we construct a single ABAC model that can do DAC, MAC, and RBAC?”
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ABAC model is not yet ready to replace DAC, MAC and/or RBAC.
ABAC can be seen as an extension of RBAC that can do MAC and DAC.
our ABAC model is the first one to cover DAC, MAC and the two variants of RBAC, and to do so in a unified manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how to build a single ABAC model with just the right features so that it can be configured to do any DAC, any MAC or any RBAC.
our ABAC model is a generalization of DAC and MAC and is a special case of RBAC.
we provide a unified ABAC model that can be configured to do DAC and RBAC, and we provide a model that can be used as a starting point for the design of a new ABAC model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ABAC model should be a generalization of DAC, MAC and role based RBAC, and that it should be easy and natural to configure the model to do DAC, RBAC and MAC.
ABAC is not a single, simple model.
ABAC can be viewed as a generalization of DAC, MAC and role based access control (RBAC).
